- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5) and prices are rising, model often underestimates the rally; increase forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates price spikes in the 10–15 day horizon; apply a 3–5% upward bias to forecasted peaks in that window.
- Model shows persistent lag in reacting to sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns positive after 3–5 days, adjust forecast to rise 2–4 days ahead of actual turn.
- Mean reversion is overestimated in model; if price is above 3σ from recent mean, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- Model often overcorrects after sharp drops; if price falls >5% from prior day, forecast next day should be 1–3% higher than prior day’s low, not lower.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate final price; add 2–5% to final forecast if sentiment remains positive or neutral over last 7 days.
